Hi Samir — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the right evaluation path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Demo recap (high level):
- FinLytics use case: regulated financial chat + document search, peak daytime volume, strict US data residency.
- You liked the fast response times in the demo and the embedding-based retrieval flow.

Key clarifying questions for engineering/ops before we map a pilot:
1) Expected sustained requests per second (RPS) and burst behaviour? (helpful to give 95th/peak estimates)
2) Latency SLO target for generation requests (ms) and for embeddings (ms).
3) Any minimum isolation or contractual needs that would force Dedicated/Private (e.g., SOC2 + on-prem requirement, or KMS/HSM)?
4) Are there internal network/VPN constraints that would prevent using our hosted endpoints?

Practical suggestion: for teams that want fastest time-to-value we recommend starting on Hosted API evaluation (short onboarding, no infra), with the option to move to Dedicated once commit/throughput is known. If data residency/workflow requires it from day one, we can look at Private (VPC) options — that typically adds 2–4 weeks for provisioning.

I attached a short quickstart checklist that lays out the Hosted pilot steps (keys, endpoints, ratecap expectations) and a matrix of rate options. Also linking the demo recording here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Aq_demo_recording

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the RPS/latency targets in a reply
- We provision a short-lived Hosted trial key and a sandbox endpoint for your engineers to test (Ben will own provisioning)
- Schedule a 30-minute ops call to walk through endpoint mapping and any perf knobs

Available times for the ops call this week: Tue/Wed 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 14:00–16:00 PT — let me know what works.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for the recap and the recording. Quick answers from my side to help you size things:

- Typical daytime sustained: 8–12 RPS for user-facing chat; embedding generation for simultaneous search jobs ~2–3 RPS.
- Bursts: marketing/process triggers can spike up to ~40 RPS for ~15–20s.
- Latency: we want 95th < 600ms for embeddings and < 1.2s for short-generation user prompts; slightly looser for longer outputs.
- Data residency: must remain within US regions; SOC2 is required but we don't strictly require on-prem at POC stage.
- VPN: we can reach hosted endpoints; corporate firewall rules are permissive after we whitelist IP ranges.

We prefer starting on Hosted to move fast, but want a clear path to Dedicated if throughput/cost suggests it. Also need clarity on per-endpoint rate limits and warm-up behavior — if a single endpoint has a small rate cap we might need multiple endpoints mapped to logical services.

Happy to take the ops call — Wed 11:00 PT works for me.

—Samir
CTO, FinLytics

Samir — great details, thanks. Short operational notes based on your numbers and our Hosted offering:

Suggested mapping for a Hosted POC:
- Generation (chat) -> single low-latency hosted endpoint with burst policy enabled. We can provision a cluster that sustains 50 RPS with auto-burst headroom for your spikes.
- Embeddings -> separate embeddings endpoint (different instance type) to isolate throughput and keep 95th low.

Rate-limit and warm-up notes:
- Per-endpoint soft rate limits are configurable on Hosted trials. Defaults are conservative; for your expected 8–12 sustained and 40 peak, we will propose a policy that sets a baseline of 25 RPS with burst to 60.
- Cold-starts are mitigated by prefix caching and an optional warm-up request script — we can provide a small script your infra team can run during load tests.

Operational next steps I will take if Wed 11:00 PT is confirmed:
1) Provision trial hosted API keys scoped to 2 endpoints (generation + embeddings) and attach a rate policy matching the numbers above.
2) Share the rate_limit_matrix.png with explicit caps and retry guidance.
3) Set up a sandbox project in HubSpot and add your infra contact so we can track capacity.

Ben (cc Priya) will be on the ops call to walk through endpoint names and the warm-up script.

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
